question: Is the Holy Spirit a person, and is he God?

answers.label: The Spirit is God, with the Father and the Son

overview.text: From the second century Christians named the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit together in worship and in defending their faith, as Athenagoras does about 177.

In the fourth century some said the Spirit was a creature. Athanasius answered that this breaks the Trinity apart, and Gregory of Nazianzus said plainly that the Spirit is God and of one substance with the Father.
The council of Constantinople in 381 confessed the Spirit as Lord and giver of life, worshipped and glorified together with the Father and the Son. Its text is listed below as a gap.

quotes.author: Athenagoras
quotes.english: Who would not be amazed to hear people called atheists who speak of God the Father, and God the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and who show both their power in unity and their distinction in order?
quotes.original: λέγοντας θεὸν πατέρα καὶ υἱὸν θεὸν καὶ πνεῦμα ἅγιον, δεικνύντας αὐτῶν καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ ἑνώσει δύναμιν καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ τάξει διαίρεσιν, ἀκούσας ἀθέους καλουμένους;
quotes.context: Romans called Christians atheists for refusing the gods. Athenagoras answers with a threefold God.

quotes.author: Spirit-fighters (Tropici), as Athanasius reports
quotes.english: A letter to Serapion, bishop of Thmuis, against those who blaspheme and say that the Holy Spirit is a creature.
quotes.original: ἐπιστολὴ πρὸς Σεραπίωνα Θμουέως ἐπίσκοπον κατὰ τῶν βλασφημούντων καὶ λεγόντων κτίσμα εἶναι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
quotes.context: The heading of Athanasius's first letter names the view he answers. Later the "Spirit-fighters" around Macedonius held a similar view; the council of 381 rejected it.

quotes.author: Athanasius of Alexandria
quotes.english: Either there is no Trinity but a pair, plus creation; or, if there is a Trinity, as indeed there is, how can they rank the Spirit of the Trinity with the creatures that come after the Trinity? That is to divide and dissolve the Trinity again. So those who think wrongly about the Holy Spirit do not think rightly about the Son either.
quotes.original: Ἢ γὰρ οὐ Τριάς ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ δυὰς, καὶ λοιπὸν ἡ κτίσις, ἢ, εἰ Τριάς ἐστιν, ὥσπερ οὖν καί ἐστι, πῶς τοῖς μετὰ τὴν Τριάδα κτίσμασι συντάττουσι τὸ τῆς Τριάδος Πνεῦμα; Τοῦτο γάρ ἐστι πάλιν διαιρεῖν καὶ διαλύειν τὴν Τριάδα. Οὐκ οῦν, κακῶς φρονοῦντες περὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὐδὲ περὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καλῶς φρονοῦσιν.
quotes.context: Written against a group in Egypt who said the Spirit was a creature, a kind of angel. The letter's heading names them.

quotes.author: Basil of Caesarea
quotes.english: For if the Lord, in handing down the saving baptism, clearly commanded his disciples to baptize all nations in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, not disdaining fellowship with him, while these men say that he must not be ranked with the Father and the Son, how do they not plainly set themselves against the ordinance of God?
quotes.original: εἰ γὰρ ὁ μὲν Κύριος σαφῶς ἐν τῇ παραδόσει τοῦ σωτηρίου βαπτίσματος προσέταξε τοῖς μαθηταῖς βαπτίζειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη εἰς ὄνομα Πατρὸς καὶ Υἱοῦ καὶ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος, οὐκ ἀπαξιῶν τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸ κοινωνίαν, οὗτοι δὲ μὴ χρῆναι αὐτὸ Πατρὶ καὶ Υἱῷ συντάσσειν λέγουσι, πῶς οὐχὶ τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ διαταγῇ προδήλως ἀνθίστανται;
quotes.context: Written in 375 against the Pneumatomachians ('Spirit fighters'). The whole argument of these chapters (15 to 19) is that the Spirit is ranked and glorified with the Father and the Son; the baptismal formula is Basil's anchor. Quoted from the PG 32 scan (poor OCR, which often reads kappa as chi); the wording is checked against Johnston's 1892 edition.

source.edition: Migne PG 32 (archive.org OCR); checked against Johnston, The Book of Saint Basil on the Holy Spirit (Oxford, 1892)

quotes.author: Gregory of Nazianzus
quotes.english: What then? Is the Spirit God? Certainly. Then is he of one substance? Yes, if he is God.
quotes.original: Τί οὖν ; θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα ; πάνυ γε. τί οὖν, ὁμοούσιον ; εἴπερ θεός.
quotes.context: Gregory preached this in Constantinople the year before the council of 381. He notes that Scripture reveals the Spirit's divinity more gradually than the Son's (31.26).

quotes.author: Council of Constantinople
quotes.english: And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life, who proceeds from the Father, who with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified together, who spoke through the prophets.
quotes.original: καὶ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, τὸ κύριον καὶ τὸ ζωοποιόν, τὸ ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον, τὸ σὺν πατρὶ καὶ υἱῷ συμπροσκυνούμενον καὶ συνδοξαζόμενον, τὸ λαλῆσαν διὰ τῶν προφητῶν
quotes.context: The creed's answer to the Spirit fighters: it does not call the Spirit God in so many words, but confesses him as Lord and giver of life, worshipped and glorified together with the Father and the Son. Text as read at Chalcedon, printed by Bright (1892).

source.edition: Bright, The Canons of the First Four General Councils (2nd ed., Oxford, 1892), Greek text

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
